officialTitle: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS assessed by blinded independent central radiologic review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: In this open-label, phase 3 trial, we randomly assigned 305 patients who had previously untreated advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 expression on at least 50% of tumor cells
design.notes: Crossover from chemotherapy to pembrolizumab permitted at progression.

clinicalQuestion: Can single-agent PD-1 blockade replace platinum doublet chemotherapy as first-line therapy for advanced NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression?

pico.population: Previously untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 expression on ≥50% of tumour cells, no sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation
pico.comparator: Investigator's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy (crossover permitted at progression)
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by blinded independent central review. Secondary: OS, ORR, safety

arms.label: Pembrolizumab
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive either pembrolizumab (at a fixed dose of 200 mg every 3 weeks)

arms.label: Platinum-based chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Investigator's choice of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy

publications.title: Pembrolizumab versus Chemotherapy for PD-L1-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: Median progression-free survival was 10.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.7 to not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 6.0 months (95% CI, 4.2 to 6.2) in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.37 to 0.68; P<0.001).
The estimated rate of overall survival at 6 months was 80.2% in the pembrolizumab group versus 72.4% in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for death, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.89; P=0.005).
The response rate was higher in the pembrolizumab group than in the chemotherapy group (44.8% vs. 27.8%)

safety.sourceQuote: treatment-related adverse events of any grade were less frequent (occurring in 73.4% vs. 90.0% of patients)
as were grade 3, 4, or 5 treatment-related adverse events (26.6% vs. 53.3%)

strengths: Randomised phase III design with PFS assessed by blinded independent central review
Biomarker-enriched population defined prospectively by PD-L1 tumour proportion score
limitations: Crossover permitted at progression, which can dilute the observed OS difference
Only patients screened with PD-L1 ≥50% were eligible; results do not extrapolate to lower PD-L1 strata

clinicalImplications.text: Established single-agent pembrolizumab as a first-line option for advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥50% and no EGFR/ALK alteration, making upfront PD-L1 testing (alongside driver profiling) standard before first-line therapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: PD-L1 ≥50% plus a negative driver panel is the entry ticket — the driver result matters first, because EGFR/ALK-positive patients were excluded.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 27718847. Updated OS analyses (e.g. 5-year) not yet ingested.
